newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-HICK MAKES POINT WITH UNBEATEN 119.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HICK MAKES POINT WITH UNBEATEN 119.

text.p: England discard Graeme Hick showed his Test career could yet be revived with an unbeaten 119 to lead Worcestershire to a convincing 85-run Sunday League win against Somerset.
Hick struck six sixes and six fours in a vintage display at Worcestershire's New Road home as his side made 262 for four.
Somerset were never in contention in response, stumbling to 177 all out in 32.2 overs.
A superb hundred from Jason Gallian ensured Lancashire stay top of the League after beating county champions Leicestershire by five wickets.
Gallian struck 104 as Lancashire recorded 259 for five in 38.4 overs in response to Leicestershire's 258 for five in a high-scoring contest at Grace Road.
Robert Croft showed his all-round qualities by striking 46 after opening the batting for Glamorgan in their six-wicket win against Durham at Pontypridd.
Croft, chosen alongside Phil Tufnell for England on Sunday, followed up the fine work of Pakistan's Waqar Younis, whose two for 28 helped restrict the visitors to 183 for eight at Pontypridd.

Australian star Matthew Hayden followed up his unbeaten double century in the championship match against Warwickshire with a sparkling 118 to give Hampshire their first Sunday win of the season by 14 runs at Southampton.
They moved off the bottom of the table after recording 278 for four, Hayden putting on 185 for the first wicket with Giles White (67).
Warwickshire were dismissed for 264 with two balls left victory.
An opening partnership of 146 between captain David Byas (72) and in-form Michael Vaughan (66) steered Yorkshire to a four-wicket win over Essex at Ilford.
Yorkshire raced to 264 for six with 19 balls remaining against an Essex total of 262 for nine that looking imposing.
Kevin Curran starred with bat and ball as Northamptonshire crushed Middlesex by 67 runs at Lord's.
Curran followed an aggressive 66 out of the visitors' seemingly below-par 198 for seven, then took four for 36 as Middlesex were bowled out for 131 in just 33.5 overs.
Only Jason Pooley offered any real resistance for the home side with 55.
Graham Cowdrey hit an enterprising 81 not out as Kent cruised past Nottinghamshire by 46 runs at Trent Bridge.
Matthew Walker, hero of Kent's memorable Benson and Hedges Cup Quarter Final victory against Warwickshire, made 78 and Nottinghamshire never looked like reaching their target.
